title: Words become vectors
lede: What happens when learning word meanings becomes cheap?
body: In 2013 Tomas Mikolov's team at Google stripped Bengio's model down to almost nothing and trained it on billions of words in under a day. The resulting vectors had a famous property: the direction from man to woman was roughly the direction from king to queen. Meaning had geometry, and anyone could compute it.

The same period produced the other half of the modern recipe. Sequence-to-sequence models read a whole sentence with one recurrent network and wrote a translation with another, end to end. And subword tokenization solved the rare-word problem by spelling unfamiliar words out of pieces. By 2016 Google had put neural translation into production.
transition: There was a flaw at the centre of sequence-to-sequence: the whole input had to fit through one fixed-size vector.
